title: Retry budget
lesson: A retry consumes the existing tool-operation budget; when it expires, runtime code blocks further attempts and reports an unknown outcome.
limitations: Illustrative CI read and runtime policy; 12 seconds, two attempts, and a two-second sampled delay are not production defaults.
The runtime gate must be implemented in code; persistent prompts do not enforce budgets or permissions.
The video does not demonstrate fleet-level jitter, write idempotency, or cancellation of remote work.
Audio analysed, not physically heard; self-reviewed, with no comparative ranking.

transcript.text: An agent asks for CI status. The runtime sends a read, receives a completed status, and returns a known result. This normal operation uses part of its own budget.
A new logical read begins. Its twelve-second shared budget starts at 00:08. The service does not reply, and the first attempt times out after five seconds.
The runtime waits two seconds before retrying. This is one illustrative sampled backoff; the shared budget continues shrinking from seven to five seconds.
The runtime sends its second and final allowed attempt. The retry uses the five seconds remaining in the original budget; the timer does not reset.
The deadline closes the runtime gate. The agent receives an unknown status. A repeated request is blocked before it reaches CI. This limits caller retries; it does not prove that remote work stopped.
